atoms.text: Fiona wrote her first article for her school’s magazine Student Monthly. Imagine you are the publisher of the magazine, and you have to edit the essay. Read through Fiona’s essay and think about the strengths and weaknesses of her argument.

instruction.text: Read Fiona’s essay and select the sentences that are irrelevant for Fiona’s argument.

atoms.b:
There_are_many_famous_women_in_history_who_worked_together_to_achieve_great_things. Their_stories_continue_to_inspire_us_to_this_day. But_I_believe_that_the_story_of_Mrs_Eliza_Ruhamah_Scidmore_and_First_Lady_Helen_Herron_Taft_is_an_especially_remarkable_reminder_of_how_far_teamwork_can_bring_us,_and_we_should_all_learn_about_their_story. These_two_women_not_only_dramatically_improved_the_landscape_of_our_capital_city,_but_also_established_a_tradition_of_US-Japan_diplomacy_that_would_define_the_countries'_relations_for_over_a_century_to_come.
Mrs_Scidmore_and_First_Lady_Taft_are_amazing_because_they_planted_cherry_blossom_trees_throughout_the_entire_city_of_Washington,_D.C. ((We all know that natural contributions are the best and most impressive contributions anyone can make to the world.))

Neither_Mrs_Scidmore_nor_First_Lady_Taft_could_have_single-handedly_designed_and_realised_the_picturesque_landscape_enjoyed_in_today’s_Washington,_D.C. Mrs_Scidmore,_a_passionate_traveler_who_had_enjoyed_many_trips_to_Japan,_visualised_how_beautiful_her_own_country’s_capital_would_look_scattered_with_pink_and_white_blossoms. She_tried_for_over_twenty_years_to_gain_support_for_her_landscaping_dream. ((Unfortunately, she was the first woman on the board of the National Geographic Society, which is obviously why she couldn’t make her dream a reality.)) Despite_her_lack_of_success,_she_never_gave_up,_and_eventually_her_idea_landed_in_the_right_hands. Mrs_Scidmore_had_written_a_letter_to_the_incoming_First_Lady,_Helen_Taft,_who_also_loved_cherry_blossoms,_having_herself_lived_in_Japan_for_a_few_years. The_First_Lady,_excited_by_this_new_image_of_the_capital_city,_immediately_put_her_political_connections_to_use. Within_three_years,_a_gift_of_3,020_cherry_blossom_trees_had_arrived_in_D.C._from_Tokyo. What_Mrs_Scidmore_and_First_Lady_Taft_each_lacked,_they_fulfilled_in_each_other_with_teamwork,_and_the_result_is_the_beautiful_city_we_see_today.

Mrs_Scidmore_and_First_Lady_Taft’s_teamwork_didn’t_only_have_a_local_effect_on_the_capital_city. These_women’s_partnership_was_essential_in_defining_US-Japan_diplomatic_relations_for_at_least_a_century_to_come. Receiving_First_Lady_Taft’s_request_for_cherry_trees_and_wanting_to_strengthen_its_relationship_with_the_US,_Japan_gave_the_trees_as_a_gift_in_1912. First_Lady_Taft’s_husband,_President_Taft,_later_sent_flowering_dogwood_trees_to_Japan_as_a_gift_of_gratitude_for_the_botanical_enrichment_of_the_city. In_1981,_a_typhoon_ravaged_much_of_Japan_and_destroyed_their_only_specimens_of_certain_types_of_cherry_blossom_trees. In_a_true_act_of_international_friendship,_the_US_identified_some_of_these_lost_species_in_the_healthy_trees_of_Washington,_D.C.,_cut_off_some_branches,_and_sent_them_back_to_Japan_so_that_they_could_reforest_their_own_cherry_trees. ((In 2019, China hosted the world’s largest gardening show, attended by more than 100 countries and international organisations, including the UK, Russia, France, and Germany.)) Mrs_Scidmore_and_First_Lady_Taft’s_partnership_had_an_even_greater_effect_than_they_had_planned:_their_work_established_a_tradition_of_botanic_diplomacy_with_Japan.

The_story_of_Mrs_Scidmore_and_First_Lady_Taft_thus_forms_a_wonderful_inspirational_tale. The_deed_of_planting_the_cherry_blossoms_in_Washington_D.C._could_not_have_been_done_by_only_one_of_these_women. They_each_brought_their_own_dreams_and_privileges_to_the_table,_and_the_result_was_greater_than_either_of_them_could_have_imagined.

b.sound: The story of Mrs Eliza Ruhamah Scidmore and First Lady Helen Herron Taft is a remarkable reminder of how far teamwork can bring us.
Japan gave the US a gift of 3,020 cherry blossom trees in 1912, hoping to strengthen the relationship between the two countries.

instruction.text: Which logical fallacy is highlighted in purple? Select the correct answer.

atoms.a: Mrs Scidmore and First Lady Taft are amazing because they planted cherry blossom trees throughout the entire city of Washington, D.C. <m-purple>We all know that natural contributions are the best and most impressive contributions anyone can make to the world.</m-purple>
b: ++This is an example of an <t-purple>appeal to nature</t-purple>.
This is an example of a <t-purple>straw man</t-purple>.

hint.text:
appeal to nature: assuming something is good because it is 'natural' or bad because it is 'unnatural'

straw man: misrepresenting an opponent’s argument, so it’s easier to argue against

finish.text: When someone <t-purple>appeals to nature</t-purple>, they claim that something is good because it is 'natural' or bad because it is 'unnatural'.
finish.sound: When someone <t-purple>appeals to nature</t-purple>, they claim that something is good because it is natural, or bad because it is unnatural.

atoms.a: Mrs Scidmore tried for over twenty years to gain support for her landscaping dream. <m-purple>Unfortunately, she was the first woman on the board of the National Geographic Society, which is obviously why she couldn’t make her dream a reality.</m-purple>
b: This is an example of an <t-purple>appeal to nature</t-purple>.

hint.text:
appeal to nature: assuming something is good because it is 'natural' or bad because it is 'unnatural'

false causation: assuming one thing caused another thing, just because they occurred together

feedback.finish: When someone uses <t-purple>false causation</t-purple>, they assume that one thing is caused by another thing just because they occurred together.

atoms.a: Mrs Scidmore and First Lady Taft’s partnership was essential in defining US-Japan diplomatic relations for at least a century to come. <m-purple>In 2019, China hosted the world’s largest gardening show, attended by more than 100 countries and international organisations, including the UK, Russia, France and Germany.</m-purple>
b: ++This is an example of a <t-purple>red herring</t-purple>.
This is an example of an <t-purple>ad hominem</t-purple> attack.

hint.text:
red herring: giving a distracting piece of information

ad hominem: attacking the person who holds a view, rather than the view itself

feedback.finish: When someone uses a <t-purple>red herring</t-purple>, they give a distracting piece of information that doesn’t actually contribute any evidence to their argument.
